passage: 'Because the initial value (Y1) and the change from initial value (Y2 - Y1) share a common variable, there is a mathematical coupling between Y1 and Y2 - Y1.' (Glossary, Europe PMC full text). Correction: 'one may assess the association between U2 - U1 and another measure obtained relatively close in time to U1 (16), e.g., a repeated measure U1bis.'
faulty: Pearson correlation between bmi_baseline (U1) and bmi_followup - bmi_baseline (U2 - U1), at most -0.25 (the crude method of the source; it is negatively biased in the source's simulations, with the expected value -1/sqrt(2) when Y1 and Y2 are uncorrelated and errors equal).
fixed: Pearson correlation between bmi_baseline_retest (U1bis) and bmi_followup - bmi_baseline (the repeated measurement method of the source), at most -0.25.
estimand: Faulty: correlation of the observed baseline with the observed change, which shares the baseline and its error. Fixed: correlation between the baseline level (measured by a second reading) and the change, whose errors are not shared; biased only toward the null by regression dilution.
model_family: The source's: linear individual growth with time, true BMI_i(t) = b0_i + b1_i*t, (b0, b1) bivariate normal (baseline mean 15.0 kg/m2, SD 1.2; yearly change mean +0.4, SD 0.2 or 0.4), measurement error normal with SD 0.3 (ICC 95%) or 1.2 (ICC 50%), ages 5 to 10. The two-wave data are the ages 5 and 10 waves plus one extra reading at age 5. The sign of the correlation of b0 and b1 is set by the world (negative for the claim-true version).
guard_minimum: 2 children (a Pearson correlation is defined from 2 observations); guards: non-finite values, selection below 2, zero variance of the baseline retest or of the change.
sizes_note: Source: 'We simulated a cohort study of 500 children' with BMI each year between ages 5 and 10; 500 children used. Source on size dependence: the bias of the crude correlation depends on measurement error variance and between-child variability of change ('The lower the correlation between Y1 and Y2, the larger is the effect of mathematical coupling'); for sample size it says only that random variability 'would have been greater for all methods with a smaller cohort size'.
exploited_structure: The change is computed from the baseline measurement and the correlation is then taken with that same baseline, so the baseline's measurement error enters both sides with opposite sign.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: 'Assuming a relatively low measurement error variance (ICC of 95%)' (Results, Relatively small change variability); the statistic is 1 - ICC, estimated from the two baseline readings, so 0.05. The larger-error scenario of the source has ICC 50% (0.5).

notes: Role: pair (CHI13 pair 1 of 2). No earlier combos for CHI13. Claim direction is negative because the source documents a negative bias of the crude estimate; the corrected estimate is attenuated toward 0 by the error in the retest reading, so the world author must keep the true correlation clearly beyond -0.25 in the claim-true version. The brief states 'five years after baseline' as the setting of the follow-up visit (source: ages 5 to 10).
